chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Kahili, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no problem with the tent upon the women and the children, and they are in Ihraam.

key_terms.مُحْرِمُونَ: in the state of Ihraam (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for women and children to stay under a tent while in Ihraam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that women and children are exempt from the prohibition of covering the head (which applies to men) during Ihraam, as the 'qubba' (canopy/tent) provides shade without constituting a head covering. This ruling highlights the distinct jurisprudential categories for genders in Hajj rituals, ensuring that the sanctity of the state is maintained while accommodating practical needs. It underscores the flexibility within Shia fiqh regarding the physical conditions of Ihraam for those not bound by the specific male prohibitions.
